_status: DRAFT, NOT IMPORTED. Second municipal-level slice in the AF branch (G.13). Sitting in src/data/research/ pending Thomas's review.
_note: Nairobi County-level finance runs on well-documented recurring instruments (a Fiscal Strategy Paper, annual Finance Acts, the national County Allocation of Revenue Act) and does depend on national fiscal-transfer law (PFM Act 2012, CARA) -- but no primary document found ties Nairobi's property rates, service tariffs, or the equitable-share transfer formula to KNBS's CPI specifically. The county's own Fiscal Strategy Paper cites KNBS's Economic Survey for its inflation chart, a different publication from the CPI report already in the corpus as `ke-knbs-cpi` -- kept as a distinct NOT-FOUND rather than loosely linked. The one genuine documented 'inflation adjustment' mechanism at Nairobi-service level is WASREB's approval of Nairobi City Water and Sewerage Company's tariff structure, which names an 'inflation adjustment' effective July 2027 but never names CPI or KNBS as its source index -- a real gap between inflation-aware and CPI-linked that is preserved here rather than papered over.

_open_questions.question: Could not locate/access the Commission on Revenue Allocation's own primary Fourth Basis formula document directly; only a Parliamentary Budget Office analytical review of the proposed framework was found and opened.

new.kenyalaw.org returned HTTP 403 to every fetch attempt for the enacted County Allocation of Revenue Act, 2025 text. The pre-enactment Senate Bill (24 June 2025) was read and quoted instead; Kenya Law's index confirms the Bill was later enacted (akn/ke/act/2025/15) but the enacted text itself was not independently verified this session.

The Nairobi City County Finance Bill, 2025 (gazetted 3 November 2025) was searched in full with no CPI/inflation mentions and does not touch land rates. No confirmation was found that it has been enacted/assented as of the research date -- treated as a Bill, not an Act.

reports.title: Nairobi City County Fiscal Strategy Paper (CFSP)
reports.publisher: Nairobi City County Treasury (County Government of Nairobi City)
reports.description: Nairobi City County's annual medium-term fiscal planning document, prepared under Public Finance Management Act, 2012 s.117: "The 2026 Nairobi County Fiscal Strategy Paper has been prepared in compliance with the requirements of the Public Finance Management Act (PFMA) 2012, Section 117 (1) and (6)." Cites the county's equitable share and conditional grant allocations from the annual County Allocation of Revenue Act. Its macroeconomic-outlook section cites "KNBS Economic survey 2025" for inflation, not a CPI report by name.
reports.cadence_note: Annual, one edition per fiscal year; required by law to be submitted by end of February each year.

reports.title: The Nairobi City County Finance Act, 2023 (No. 4 of 2023)
reports.description: Nairobi City County's Finance Act amending the Nairobi City County Revenue Act, 2015, including the land-rates schedule. Sets a flat late-payment interest of "three percent (3%) per month" on overdue property rates, computed as simple interest -- a fixed penalty, not a CPI-indexed rate. Property valuations continue to reference the 2019 valuation roll under the (since-repealed) Valuation for Rating Act Cap 266.

reports.title: National Rating Act, 2024 (No. 15 of 2024)
reports.publisher: Republic of Kenya / National Council for Law Reporting (Kenya Gazette Supplement No. 218, Acts No. 15)
reports.region: Kenya (applies to all 47 counties including Nairobi City County)
reports.description: National framework law for property valuation and rating, replacing the former Rating Act (Cap 267) and Valuation for Rating Act (Cap 266): "The Rating Act and the Valuation for Rating Act are hereby repealed." Requires a valuation roll "every five years" and defines the tax rate as set "from time to time by a county government" -- no CPI or inflation index appears anywhere in the Act.

reports.title: The County Allocation of Revenue Bill / Act, 2025 (No. 9 of 2025, Senate)
reports.publisher: Republic of Kenya, Senate / National Treasury (Kenya Gazette Supplement No. 95, Senate Bills No. 9 of 2025)
reports.region: Kenya (allocates to all 47 counties, including Nairobi City County by name)
reports.description: Annual law dividing counties' equitable share of nationally-raised revenue. First Schedule names "Nairobi City" specifically with a total equitable share allocation of Ksh 21,417,128,397. The macro assumption underlying the aggregate national-to-county pool states inflation is assumed to "remain stable within the government target" range -- a planning assumption for the overall pool, not a per-county CPI-indexed formula term.
reports.cadence_note: Enacted annually alongside the Division of Revenue Act, ahead of each new financial year (1 July).

reports.title: Review of the Proposed 4th Basis of Sharing Revenue Among Counties
reports.publisher: Parliamentary Budget Office (PBO), Parliament of Kenya
reports.region: Kenya (all 47 counties; discusses Nairobi City County specifically as a case example)
reports.description: Parliamentary Budget Office review of the Commission on Revenue Allocation's proposed Fourth Basis equitable-share formula: five parameters -- "Equal Share (22%), Population (42%), Geographical Size (9%), Poverty (14%), and Income Distance (13%)." Names Nairobi specifically as an example of the population parameter's daytime/night-time census measurement difficulty. Discusses inflation only in general macroeconomic narrative, separate from and not incorporated into the formula's weighting.

reports.title: Nairobi City Water and Sewerage Company Limited Approved Tariff Structure, FY2025/26–2028/29 (Gazette Notice No. 2710)
reports.publisher: Water Services Regulatory Board (WASREB), approving Nairobi City Water and Sewerage Company Limited's (NCWSC) tariff application
reports.description: WASREB-approved water/sewerage tariff structure for Nairobi's city water utility (NCWSC), a county-owned utility distinct from Nairobi City County government itself. Section 1.3 'Indexation': "The utility's approved tariffs for water and sewerage shall be eligible for annual indexation, as per the regulations of the Water Services Regulatory Board (WASREB). The inflation adjustment shall come into effect every July of the tariff period commencing July 2027." No specific index (e.g. CPI/KNBS) is named anywhere in the notice.

reports.title: Public Finance Management Act, 2012 (No. 18 of 2012)
reports.description: National framework law governing national and county public finance, including the Division of Revenue Bill / County Allocation of Revenue Bill process and the requirement that county Fiscal Strategy Papers be prepared under s.117. Full-text search of the Act found no mention of "Consumer Price Index", "CPI", "inflation", or "KNBS" anywhere, including in the equitable-share/Division-of-Revenue provisions.
